Coal Bed Methane Policy  
*322. SHRI MAHMOOD A. MADANI: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a)  the salient features of the Coal Bed Methane Policy 1997; 
(b)  the details of blocks awarded tor the exploration and production; 
(c)  the basis of awarding such blocks; 
(d)  whether the exploration in all the blocks have been completed; 
(e)  if so, the details of the blocks, capacity-wise; and 
(t) in how many blocks commercial production has started and how is it being utilized? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): 
a) to (f) Government of India approved Coal Bed Methane (CBM) Policy in 1997 to harness 
the resource of CBM gas in the country. Implementation commenced in 2001 by offering 
CMB blocks in first round of CBM policy. Till date, three rounds of CBM policy have been 
concluded. The salient features of CBM policy are given at Statement (See below). 
Under this policy, Government of India has awarded 23 CBM blocks to Indian and foreign 
companies on equal terms and conditions through int ernational competitive bidding 
system i a transparent manner. In addition to 23 CBM blocks, Government of India had also 
awarded blocks on nomination basis to Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) 
and Coal 

Written Answers to  [15 APRIL 2008]  Starred Questions   5 
India Limited (CIL) as well as 1 block to Great Eastern Energy Corporation Limited (GEECL) 
through Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) r oute. Thus, 26 CBM blocks have 
been contracted till date. These blocks are located  in the states of Andhra Pradesh (2), 
Chhattisgarh (3), Gujarat (1), Jharkhand (6), Madhy a Pradesh (5), Maharashtra (1), 
Rajasthan (4) and West Bengal (4). 
Under third round of CBM policy, Bids were evaluated on a scale of 100 points based on 
three main criteria, viz., Technical Capability (20 points), committed work program for the 
block (45 points) and fiscal package (35 points). B id Evaluation Criteria were totally 
quantified and made available to the bidders mrough  Notice Inviting Offer (NIO) before 
submitting the bids. Technical capability criterion included operatorship experience, acreage 
holding, reserves and annual production of the oper ator. Work programme included the 
minimum commitment by the operator for carrying out exploration and pilot assessment in 
the block. Fiscal package indicated the offered Government take. CBM blocks were awarded 
to the bidders getting highest points out of 100 points. 
CBM Exploration period has been divided into two parts, viz., (i) Phase-I up to 3 years 
and (ii) Phase II up to 5 years including pilot ass essment and market confirmation. As of 
date, 3 CBM blocks are in development and productio n stage and remaining blocks are in 
different exploration phases. 
In 26 CBM blocks, 1453 billion cubic metres (BCM) of resources were estimated at the 
time of offer of these blocks. Block-wise resource estimates are at the Statement-II (See 
below) In four blocks, CBM gas reserves of the orde r of 176 billion cubic metres (BCM) 
have been established by GEECL, ONGC and Reliance Industries Limited (RIL). 
First commercial production of CBM gas by GEECL commenced in July, 2007 in Raniganj 
located in West Bengal. The gas produced is being supplied to local industries in the vicinity 
of the block. 
Statement-I 
The salient features of CBM policy  
The successful bidder would be required to enter in to a contract with the Government, 
which will be negotiated based on the Model Contrac t (MC). Some of the features of the 
attractive terms offered by the Government are: 
(i) No signature bonus. 
(ii) Royalty at the rate of 10% on the value of CBM  in accordance with Oilfield 
(Regulation and Development) Act, 1948 and the Rules framed thereunder payable 
to the relevant State Government. 
(iii) Additionally, ad-valorem biddable Production Leval Payment (PLP), payable to the 
Central Government, on every incremental production of zero point five (0.5) Million 
Standard Cubic Metre per Day (MMSCMD) or part there of. 
(iv) Freedom to market gas in domestic market at market determined prices. 
(v) Fiscal stability provision in the contract. 
(vi) No customs duty on imports required for CBM op erations. 
(vii) Provisions for assignment of Participating Interest.

Petronet LNG terminal at Kochi 
*323. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of  PETROLEUM AND 
•JATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether statutory approvals for the project Petrone t LNG terminal at Kochi have 
•been granted; 
(b)  the details of the pre-project activities; 
(c)  whether the arrangement for gas supply has been finalized; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof; 
(e)  whether there is any further formalities to be completed prior to the commissioning of 
he project; 
(f)  if so, details thereof; 
(g) whether there is any time-frame fixed for the commissioning of the project; and 
(h) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): 
a) Petronet LNG Limited (PLL) has obtained the necessary statutory approvals in respect 
of Kochi terminal. Approvals in respect of the Concession Agreement and the Land Lease 
Agreement with Cochin Port Trust have yet to be obt ained. 
(b) The following pre-project activities in respect  of the LNG terminal at Kochi have 
been completed: 
1.  Land Survey and Soil Investigation. 
2.  Seabed Engineering and Oceanographic Investigations. 
3.  Marine Geo-technical Investigations. 
4.  Rapid and Comprehensive Marine and Terrestrial Environmental Impact Assessment 
Study. 
5.  Physical and Mathematical Model Studies. 
6.  Marine and Terrestrial Risk Analysis. 
7.  Detailed Feasibility Report. 
8.  Basic Engineering Package. 
(c) and (d) PLL is in advanced stage of discussions for the supply of LNG from Gorgon 
project, Australia. 
(e) to (h) Formalities relating to, inter-alia, execution of Concession Agreement and Land 
Lease Agreement are required to be completed before the commissioning of me Kochi LNG 
project. The project is estimated for mechanical completion around fourth quarter of 2011.

*324. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased 
:co state:

(a)  whether Government proposes to give any package to the State Government of Goa to 
give a boost to the tourism industry there; 
(b)  whether Government proposes to approve any special project proposed by the State 
Government in this regard; 
(c)  whether the proposed tourism policy of Government has been finalized; and

THE MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI): (a)  and (b) The 
development and promotion of places of tourist interest is primarily undertaken by the State 
Governments themselves. However, Ministry of Touris m provides funds on the basis of 
projects prioritised in consultation with the State  Governments every year for Product/ 
Infrastructure development of tourist destinations/circuits. The project proposals which are 
complete in all respect, are appraised on the basis  of inter-se-prioriry and funds released,

During the year 2007-08, five project proposals for grant of Central Financial Assistance

guidelines and hence these could not be sanctioned. However, during the Tenth Plan period, 
projects worth Rs. 157.26 lakh were sanctioned for integrated development of tourism in the 
State of Goa. 
(c) and (d) The National Tourism Policy has been formulated in the year 2002 to position 
tourism as a major engine of economic growth, to harness the direct and multiplier effects of 
tourism on employment generation, economic developm ent and poverty eradication in an 
environmentally sustainable manner and to create an d develop tourism infrastructure in 
partnership with States, private sector and other agencies.

Non-availability of institutional lending sources for farmers  
*326. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether Government is aware that around 52 per cent farmers do not have access to 
institutional sources like banks and cooperatives; 
(b)  if so, whether Government is aware that most of the  farmers take loan from the 
moneylenders; 
(c)  if so, whether Government proposes to regulate the banking business being done by 
these moneylenders and get them registered with the  Reserve Bank of India to carry on 
banking business and also regulate the interest rates; and 
(d)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) and (b) As per National 
Sample Survey Organisation data on 'Indebtedness of Farmer Households' (2003), 51.4% of 
farmer households do not access credit, either from institutional or non-institutional sources. 
27.30% of total farm households are indebted to for mal sources and 21.3% to informal 
sources, including moneylenders. 
(c) and (d) As per the VIIth Schedule of the Consti tution of India, 'money-lending and 
moneylenders', are included in the State List at En try No. 30. A majority of the State 
Governments have State Moneylenders'Acts in place for regulating the activity of money-
lending in their area. 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) set-up a Technical Grou p to review the efficacy of the 
existing legislative framework that governs money-lending as also the enforcement machinery 
in different States and make recommendations for its improvement. The model legislation 
proposed by the Technical Group, inter-alia, provides for the following: 
* a simple and hassle free procedure for compulsory registration and periodical renewal 
of their registration by moneylenders; 
* a simplified dispute resolution mechanism to ensure better enforcement; 
* adoption of the rule of' 'Damdupat', i.e. the interest charged should not exceed the 
Principal. 
RBI has sent the Report to all the State Governments as part of its process of consultation. 
Zonal Cultural Centres 
*327. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a)  what is the mandate of Zonal Cultural Centres; 
(b)  whether any study has been done on the performance of such Zonal Cultural Centres 
against their mandate; 
(c)  if so, the details of such study; 
(d)  whether it is a fact that the Zonal Cultural Centres are facing resource crunch; 
(e)  if so, the annual allocation for the last three years, Centre-wise; and

(f) the details of quarter-wise release of Plan and Non-Plan funds to each of the Centre 
during the financial year 2007-08? 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI): (a) The Government of 
India has set up seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs ) in various parts of the country to 
extend support to folk and traditional artistes and artisans of the country. 
(b)  Yes, Sir. 
(c)  A Committee under the Chairmanship of Prof. U.R. An antha Murthy was set up in 
1994 to review the functioning of these Zonal Cultu ral Centres. The terms of reference of 
the Committee were as follows:— 
(i) To review the working of the seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) with reference to 
the objectives for which they were set up; 
(ii) Suggest how they can even better serve the purpose of enriching and strengthening 
the cultural patterns in their respective areas of operation; 
(iii) Suggest ways and means for adequate and effective networking with similar State/ 
Central bodies and other cultural institutions of eminence in the country; 
(iv) Suggest ways of developing, involving the artistic community in the total literacy 
campaign leading to a kind of cultural resurgence in the country. 
The Committee, in its report recommended greater ou treach, more emphasis on tribal/ 
folk art, documentation of rare and vanishing arts forms, better co-ordination with National 
and State Akademies and patronage to young and upcoming artistes. 
As a follow up to these recommendations, new schemes directly funded by the Ministry 
of Culture have been introduced. These include Theatre Rejuvenation Scheme, Guru Shishya 
Parampara Scheme and Young Talented Artistes Scheme. 
(d)  No, Sir. 
(e)  Does not arise.

Difference in inflation rates  
*329. SHRI PENUMALLIMADHU: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a)  the reasons for the difference in the inflation rates between Wholesale Price Index and 
Consumer Prices Indices; and 
(b)  what are the steps/changes proposed to narrow the difference? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) and (b) The differences 
in the inflation rates between Wholesale Price Inde x and Consumer Price Indices reflect 
differences in the base year, commodity basket and weighting patterns relevant for different 
target groups of consumers. The commodity basket and weights for the respective Consumer 
Price Indices are derived on the basis of group-specific consumer expenditure surveys. The 
Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is an economy wide index covering 435 commodities. Weights 
of these commodities are derived based on the value  of quantities traded in the domestic 
market. It is a more comprehensive measure of economy-wide inflation available with high 
frequency. In view of this, no steps as such can be taken to "narrow" the difference.

Construction of river valley project  
†*334. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN SHARMA: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a)  the reasons for increase in salinity of the soil in  the regions of river valley projects 
constructed under First and Second Five Year Plans; 
(b)  the steps being taken to check it; 
(c)  whether situation will improve with the implementation of river linking projects; and 
(d)  if not, the reasons for not stopping the work on river linking projects? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ): (a) With the 
start of the planned irrigation development in the post independence era, farmers started 
using irrigation water in the irrigated commands. In areas, where drainage was not adequate, 
this resulted in the rise of ground water table and  the seepage from unlined canals further 
contributed to the problem. The rise in ground wate r table brought the excessive harmful 
salts on the land surface causing salinity. 
(b) Both preventive as well as ameliorative measures are being laken to check salinity. 
The preventive measures include lining of canals in vulnerable reaches, On-Farm development 
works such as construction of lined field channels and field drains, rotational supply 
(warabandi) of irrigation water to farmers, conjunc tion use of surface and ground water, 
propagation of improved methods of irrigation among  farmers through training, adaptive 
trials and demonstrations. 
Ameliorative measures include construction of surface and sub-surface drains, vertical 
drainage and bio-drainage for disposal of excess wa ter and leaching of soils to flush out 
excess salts from root zone of crops. 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The proposed interlinking of rivers is a part of National Perspective 
Plan formulated by Ministry of Water Resources and Central Water Commission in 1980 
which would provide many benefits such as increase in irrigated area, generation of hydro 
power, flood moderation, navigation, water supply, pollution control and control of salinity.

Operation of National Aviation Company of India Ltd.  
2338. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of CIVILAVIATION be pleased 
to state: 
(a)  whether Government has taken steps to implement agr eements that had  been allied 
with employees related to wages and cadre policy etc.; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d)  the steps taken in detail to earmark aviation polic y to make a stiff competition to 
private operators, by the National Aviation Company of India Ltd. (NACIL) as per the market 
dynamics? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIA TION (SHRI 
PRAFUL PATEL): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Agreements/Set tlements reached with the 
Unions/Associations of both the erstwhiie companies are in the process of implementation. 
Revision of pay scales have been affected in respec t of all employees represented by five 
Unions/Associations, which have arrived at an understanding with the management, and the 
executives of the erstwhile Indian airlines. The ar rears of wages have been paid/are being 
paid as per the agreements and action has been init iated to implement the settlement/ 
understanding on career progression. In respect of erstwhile Air India, in most of the cases 
where agreements/settlements have been signed, wage arrears or advance have been paid. 
(c)  Does not arise. 
(d)  Merger of Air India Limited and Indian Airlines Lim ited into National Aviation 
Company of Indian Limited has been effected to impr ove the operational performance/ 
profitability and to face the increasing competition in the aviation market. The merger has 
the potential to provide substantial synergy for procurement, sales and distribution besides 
affording an opportunity for financial restructurin g/strengthening by leveraging common 
assets. Further, the airlines have been permitted t o add more capacity by purchasing 111 
state-of-the-art new aircraft. Other commercial mea sures such as route rationalization 
alongwith introduction of services on new routes, product improvement and joining of "Star 
Alliance" have also been taken by NACIL to effectively face composition.

FDI in Aviation Sector 
2341. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the Minister of CIV1L AVIATION be pleased to 
state: 

Written Answers to  [15 APRIL 2008]  Unstarred Questions    33 
(a)  whether Government has taken a decision to open var ious sectors in Civil Aviation 
Industry to FDI and also to rationalize the FDI norms in this regard; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d)  the manner in which Government proposes to safeguard the interests of the domestic 
airlines? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIA TION (SHRI 
PRAFUL PATEL): (a) to (c) The Government has taken decision on Policy for Foreign Director 
Investment (FDI) in Civil Aviation Sector as under:— 
Airports: (i) Greenfield Projects: FDI upto 100% is allowed under the automatic route. 
(ii) Existing projects? FDI upto 100% is allowed with prior approval of the Government for 
FDI beyond 74%. 
Air Transport Services: (i) Scheduled Air Transport Service/Domestic Schedu led 
Passenger Airline? FDI upto 49% and investment by Non-Resident Indians (NRI) upto 100% 
allowed on the automatic route. 
(ii) Non-Scheduled Air Transport Service/Non-Scheduled airlines, Chartered airlines and Cargo 
airlines: FDI upto 74% and investment by Non-Resident Indians (NRI) upto 100% allowed on 
the automatic route. 
(iii) Helicopter services/seaplane services requiring DGCA approval? FDI upto 100% 
allowed on the automatic route. 
Other services under Civil Aviation Sector: (i) Ground Handling Services: FDI upto 74% and 
investment by Non-Resident Indians (NRI) upto 100% allowed on the automatic route. This will 
be subject to sectoral regulations and security clearance. 
(ii) Maintenance and Repair organizations; flying training institutes; and technical training 
institutions? FDI upto 100% allowed on the automatic route. 
(d) The new FDI policy will not affect the domestic scheduled airlines as it does not allow 
foreign airlines to participate directly or indirectly in the FDI. The same applies for non-
scheduled and chartered operations.

Loss in valuation of exchange rate 
2371. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a report of RBI has shown that the valuation loss between the 
March Exchange Rate and September Exchange Rate is around Rs. 92383 crores and the 

52    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
valuation loss between the June Exchange Rate and December Exchange Rate is around 
Rs. 31143 crores;  
(b)  whether this kind of situation would ever occur or have occurred in any other country; 
and 
(c)  if so, how did they manage while India could not do it? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN 
KUMAR BANSAL): (a) to (c) Gains/losses on valuation of foreign currency assets and 
gold due to movements in the exchange rates and/or prices of gold are not taken to Profit and 
Loss Account of the RBI, but instead booked under a balance sheet head named as Currency 
and Gold Revaluation Account (CGRA). The balance represents accumulated net gain on 
valuation of foreign currency assets and gold. At the year-end, assets and liabilities in foreign 
currencies are translated at the exchange rates prevailing on the last business day except in 
cases where rates are contractually fixed. Exchange gains and losses arising from translation 
of foreign currency assets and liablities, which are essentially holding gains and not actual 
gains, are accounted for in CGRA and remain adjusted therein. The above reflects prudent 
accounting practice for Central Banks. The Annual Report of Reserve Bank of India for the 
year 2006-07 indicates the balances in the CGRA as at the end of June 30 were Rs. 51,276.41 
crore in 2002-03, Rs. 62,283.04 crore in 2003-04, Rs. 26,906.21 crore in 2004-05, 
Rs. 86,789.18 crore in 2005-06 and Rs. 21,723.52 crore in 2006-07. As the US dollar —a 
widely held reserve currency — is depreciating against other major currencies, similar 
valuation losses could be reported in the balance sheets of the Central Banks of other countries, 
for which no separate information is available with the Government of India.

Statement  
Details of Guidelines for Selection of Part-time Non-Official Director  
The following criteria may be adopted for nomination of part-time non-official directors (NOD) 
on the boards of public sector banks/financial institutions etc. 
(I) GENERAL 
1.  Nominations will be made keeping in view the provis ions of the relevant Acts/ 
Rules. 
2.  The suitability of nominees may be assessed in term s of formal qualification and 
expertise, track record, integrity etc. For assessing integrity and suitability, information on 
criminal records, financial position, civil actions undertaken to pursue personal debts, 
refusal of admission to or expulsion from professional bodies, sanctions applied by 
regulators and similar bodies and previous questionable business practices etc. will be 
relied upon. 
3.  Persons with special academic training or practical  experience in the fields of 
agriculture, rural economy, banking, cooperation, economics, business management, 
human resources, finance, law, marketing, industry and IT will ordinarily be 
considered. 
4.  As far as possible representation may also be given  to women and the persons 
belonging to SC/ST community. 
(II) EDUCATION 
1. An NOD should at least be a graduate Educational qualifications may be relaxed with 
the approval of ACC in case of farmers, depositors and artisans. 
(Ill) AGE 
1. The age of the Director, on the date of recommendation by Appointments Board , 

72    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
should not be less than 40 years and preferably bel ow 60 years. The upper age 
limit may be relaxed in case of outstanding experts, eminent persons. 
(IV) WORK  EXPERIENCE 
1. professionals/academicians should ordinarily have 10 years of work experience in 
the particular field. 
(V) DISQUALIFICATION 
1.  A director already on a Bank/FI, under any category , may not be considered for 
nomination as NOD on any other Bank/FI. 
2.  Persons connected with hire purchase, financing, investment, leasing and other para-
banking activities, MPs, MLAs, MLCs and Stock Brokers will not be appointed as 
non-official directors on the boards of Banks/FIs. 
3.  No person may be re-nominated as a NOD on the Board of a Bank/FI on which he/ 
she has served as Director in the past under any category for two terms or six years 
whichever is longer. 
4.  An NOD would not be considered for nomination as a Director on the Board of a 
Bank/FI if such Director has already been a NOD/shareholder/Director on the board 
of any other Bank/FI for six years, whether continuously or intermittently. 
(VI) PROFESSIONAL  RESTRICTION 
1.  NOD will not accept/will not be allotted any work of the Bank/FI for two years after 
demitting office as Director of that Bank/FI. 
2.  During his term as NOD on any Bank, such Director w ill not undertake any 
professional work (statutory audit, concurrent audit, legal retainership or empanelment 
as a lawyer etc.) in any other Public Sector Bank. In the case of SBI, such restrictions 
will cover Associate Banks as well. However, in respect of any other bank/insurance 
company, the firm should be allowed to be engaged, provided the non official director 
recuses himself/herself from handling that part of the business of the firm, where 
there may be a conflict of interest. 
3.  If a person having professional relationship with bank, including cooperative bank, 
is selected for being nominated on the board of any bank, he will have to sever his 
connection with the bank before such appointment. 
4.  Professionals shall not be nominated on the Board o f a PSB with which they have 
had a business relationship during the last 3 years before such nomination. 
(VII ) REGIONAL  REPRESENTATION 
Effort should be made to ensure representation of a ll the six zones of the country-
North, South, East, West, Central and North-East — on the Boards of Public Sector 
Banks taken together.

In the Mid-Term Review of annual Policy Statement (dated October 30, 2007), RBI has 
observed that in view of the rise in the number of litigations against banks for engaging 
recovery agents in the recent past, it is felt that the adverse publicity could result in serious 
reputational risk for the banking sector as a whole. RBI has urged banks to follow prescribed 
guidelines while engaging recovery agents and has clarified that complaints received regarding 
abusive practices followed by a bank's recovery age nt would invite serious supervisory  
reisapproval. RBI would considef imposing a temporary ban (or even a permanent ban in case of 
persistent abusive practices), for engaging recovery agents, on those banks where strictures have 
been passed/penalities have been imposed by a High Court/Supreme Court or against its 
Directors/Officers with regard to the abusive practices followed by their recovery agents. 
RBI has also placed on its website, on 30th November, 2007, draft Guidelines for Banks 
engaging Recovery Agents for feed back. Based on th e feedback received from banks/ 
individuals/organisations, the guidelines have been  revised and a second draft has been 
issued on 25th March, 2008 for feedback. These guidelines cover various operational issues 
concerning engagement of recovery agents by the ban ks, methods to be followed by them 
for recovery of dues, training for the recovery age nts, procedure for taking possession of 
property mortgaged/hypothecated to the banks, etc. The banks have also been advised to 
strictly abide by the codes pertaining to collection of dues.

exploration; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL 
GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PATEL): (a) to (d) Yes, Sir. In  order to adopt a transparent and 
consistent framework for granting extensions in exploration phases, the Government in line 
with the existing policy of extensions under NELP and pre-NELP contracts, has framed an 
extension policy for considering proposals seeking extension in exploration phases under 
CBM contracts. The extension in phases under CBM co ntracts in terms of this policy 
framework would be considered within the validity of the over all exploration period. The 
broad objective of the extension policy is as under:— 
(i) To maintain the integrity of the bidding proces s and the spirit of the contracts to 
explore and produce CBM gas early. 
(ii) To grant reasonable extension of time so as to enable contractors to complete Minimum 
Work Programme (MWP) or additional exploration work programme. 
(iii) Not to delay the execution of development plans or production or the life cycle of the 
entire project and payment of Royalty, taxes and contractual payments. 
(iv) To act as deterrent for seeking unnecessary ex tensions or holding on to acreages 
without doing any or little exploration activities.

is for completing MWP or additional Work Programme,  whether commerciality has been 
established in the contract area and whether contra ctor wants to retain the area for further 
exploration have been kept in mind.

on merit in terms of the provisions of the respective contracts.

which are not attributable to the contractors will be counted as excusable delays and such

period or extended period, as the case may be, he s hall be required to pay money for the 
unfinished work programme, if any, to the Government in terms of respective provisions of 
the contract. 
Government of India has signed contracts for 26 CBM  blocks (including award of 3

promoting value addition in refining for making the  country an export hub of petroleum 
products, the proposed changes will have repercussi ons on the country's PSU refineries 
and the E & P sector besides having a negative impa ct on the country's energy security 
efforts.

the ongoing expansion and upgradation projects which are scheduled to commence refining

proposed in the Finance Bill, 2008, the tax holiday benefit would cease to be available for

2441. DR. V. MAITREYAN: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government has drawn up a unique well planned programme 
to automate the various petrol pumps across the country by the Oil Marketing Companies; 
(b)  if so, the status of this automation; 
(c)  the total plan outlay for this programme; 
(d)  wheher it is also a fact that plan is running behind schedule; 
(e)  the reasons for this delay and by when the completi on of this automation will take 
place; and 
(f) the main benefits to the common customers due to this automation process? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL 
GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PATEL): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. In order to monitor the activities at 
Retail Outlets (ROs) by adopting the latest technol ogical improvements, Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) have been advised to expeditiously complete the Automation of ROs 
selling more than 200 KL per month. 
As on 31.03.2008, OMCs have completed approx 70% au tomation of the ROs selling 
more than 200 KL per month. 
(c)  Total plan outlay for this programme of OMCs is 682.71 Crores. 
(d)  and (e) BPCL has completed the automation programme as per their target HPCL and 
IOCL have not completed the automation of all ROs as per schedule, i.e. 31.03.2008. They 
are expecting to complete the automation of balance ROs by September, 2008. OMCs have 
reported that the following are the factors affecting the pace of automation: 
(i) The retail automation is a niche segment and globally only limited vendors are 
available to carry out system integration for retail automation. 
(ii) Wide geographical spread of the ROs to be automated across the country creating 
logistics strain; 
(iii) High import content requirement both in hardware as well as software.

monitoring of the stocks, receipts and sales from t he automated retail outlets, apart from 
other features like computerized billing etc. These transactions are constantly recorded by 
the system and are automatically transferred to OMC s Head Office on daily bdsis. The 
system is expected to ensure efficient stock reconciliation on day-to-day basis thereby reducing 
the chances of unintended product being unloaded in the tanks at these retail outlets.

Taxes on petrol and diesel 
2452. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA: Will the Minister of PETR OLEUM AND NATURAL 
GAS be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether it is a fact that there is a proposal to cut taxes on petrol and diesel; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether consumers have to bear the burden of the increasing crude oil prices; and 
(d)  if so, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL 
GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PATEL): (a) and (b) In the Union Budget 2008-09, the ad-valorem 
component of excise duty on unbranded petrol and unbranded diesel has been abolished and 
converted to a specific duty of Rs. 14.35 and Rs. 4.60 per litre respectively, with effect from 
1.3.2008. 
(c) and (d) The international prices of crude oil a nd petroleum products have remained 
high and volatile since 2004. As passing on the entire impact of the increase in the oil prices 
to the consumers would have resulted in acute hardship to the common man, the retail selling 
prices of sensitive petroleum products namely petrol, diesel, domestic LPG and PDS kerosene 
have not been increased in tandem with the international oil prices. Due to this, the Public 
Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) are incurring under-recoveries on domestic sale 
of these sensitive petroleum products. To deal with the steep escalation in international oil 
prices, the Government has adopted the principle of "equitable burden sharing" between the 
Government, the oil PSUs and consumers to protect the interests of the common man and 
vulnerable sections of society, as also the financial health of OMCs. 
In this context, the Government has made a marginal increase in petrol and diesel prices 
by Rs. 2/litre and Re. 1 /litre respectively with effect from 15.2.2008, which is actually in the 
nature of a restoration of the retail prices of the se products to the price level operating 
before February, 2007. Even after this, it is estimated that the OMCs have suffered under-
recoveries of over Rs. 70,000 crore on the sale of these products during 2007-08. Despite 
the steep increase in the international oil prices, the prices of domestic LPG and PDS Kerosene 
have not been increased since November, 2004 and Ma rch, 2002 respectively. The 
Government has issued Oil Bonds and the Upstream Oil Companies have also contributed 
by offering discounts on crude oil and petroleum products to partially compensate the under-

recoveries of OMCs and to protectthe consumers from the adverse effect of rising international 
oil prices.

Programme for flood control  
t2474. SHRI JAI PARKASH AGGARWAL: Will the Minister  of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government has taken or proposes to take any steps to formulate  a 
comprehensive programme for carrying the water from frequently, flooded parts of the 
country and surplus water flowing in rivers to drought prone areas and also to control 
floods in vast areas; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, as on date; and 
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI 
JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (c) The Ministry of Water Resources 
(erstwhile Ministry of Irrigation) and Central Wate r Commission formulated a 
National Perspective Plan (NPP) for Water Resources Development in 1980. The NPP 
comprises of two components viz. (i) Peninsular Rivers Development and (ii) Himalayan 
Rivers Development and envisages construction of storages on various river systems 
along with interlinking canal systems to transfer water from water surplus areas to 
water deficit regions. National Water Development Agency (NWDA) was set up in 
1982 to study the feasibility of Interbasin water transfer proposals and give a concrete 
shape to NPP. The Inter-linking proposals under NPP" envisages additional benefits of 
25 million ha. of irrigation from surface waters, 1 0 million ha. by increased use of 
ground waters and generation of 34,000 MW of power apart from the incidental 
benefits of flood moderation, navigation, water supply, salinity and pollution control 
etc.  
Based on various studies conducted, NWDA has identified 30 links (16 links under 
Peninsular Component and 14 links under Himalayan Component) for preparation of 
Feasibility Reports (FRs). Out of these, FRs of 14 links under Peninsular Component and 
2 links (Indian portion) under Himalayan Component have already been completed. NWDA 
has taken up the work of Preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) for one priority link 
viz. Ken—Betwa under Peninsular Component.

NWDA Award and Hon'ble Supreme Court.

help the affected families.

2006 in Writ Petition No. 328 of 2002 against the Union of India & Others in the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court of India regarding serious violations of R&R of Project Affected Families 
(PAFs). On the date of hearing of the above Writ Petition on 10.3.2008, the Hon'ble Supreme 
Court passed the Order that the State of Madhya Pradesh should file response by way of 
affidavit to the suggestions made by the NCA. As the above case is still pending in the

Sanction of irrigation projects in Gujarat  
2480. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL: Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to 
state: 
(a)  whether minor and medium irrigation projects of Gujarat sanctioned under Ninth and 
Tenth Five Year Plans with the Central assistance could not be implemented; 
(b)  if so, the names of the projects; 
(c)  the reasons for non-implementation of these projects; and 
(d)  which projects of Gujarat under these plans could n ot be sanctioned for want of 
environmental clearance? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES (SHRI 
JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) In Gujarat, 8 medium irrigation projects have 
been sanctioned during Ninth and one medium project has been sanctioned during Tenth Five 
Year Plans with Central assistance under Accelerate d Irrigation Benefits Programme 
(AJBP). No minor irrigation project/scheme of Gujarat has been sanctioned under AIBP. 
Of the above 9 medium projects, five projects have been completed and reamaining 4 are 
under implementation by the Government of Gujarat. 
Government of Gujarat has informed that no project has been held up for Central assistance 
for want of environmental clearance. 
Flood relief  
2481. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA TAIMUR: Will the Minist er of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
; (a) whether Government proposes to pump Rs. 8000 crore into flood relief in the Eleventh 
Five Years Plan; 
(b) if so, whether it would suffice in view of aver age annual loss of 1000 lives and 
Rs. 1800 crore worth of properties, including crops due to perennial floods; and 
(c) whether fool-proof flood management techniques would be evolved and their effective 
implementation ensured by State and district authorities, as past flood relief schemes suffered 
due to lack of co-ordination? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES (SHRI 
JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) No Sir. However a s tate sector scheme, 
namely "Flood Management Programme" for providing C entral assistance to the State 
Governments to undertake flood control and river ma nagement works in critical reaches 
amounting to Rs. 8000 crores has been approved 'in principle' by the Government for Eleventh 
Plan period in November, 2007. 
(b)  Does not arise. 
(c)  The flood management schemes are planned, investiga ted and implemented by the 
State Governments; which are appraised by State TAC, Central agencies like Central Water 
Commission and Ganga Flood Control Commission and Advisory Committee of the Union 
Ministry of Water Resources, depending upon the cost of the scheme(s), as per the guidelines 
of Planning Commission.

DISQUALIFICATION OF A MEMBER ON GROUND OF DEFECTION 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I have to make the following announcement: 
Shrimati Sushma Swaraj, Member, Rajya Sabha, filed before the then Chairman, Rajya 
Sabha, Shri Bhairon Singh Shekhawat, petition dated December 22,2005, under paragraph 
6 of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution and rul e 6 of the members of Rajya Sabha 
(Disqualification on ground of Defection) Rules, 19 85, praying that the Chairman, Rajya 
Sabha, be pleased to hold that Shri Jai Narain Prasad Nishad, Member, Rajya Sabha, stands 
disqualified under theTenth Schedule to the Constitution of India and also declare his seat 
in the Rajya Sabha vacant. 
The then Chairman forwarded copies of the petition and the annexures thereto to Shri Jai 
.Narain Prasad Nishad and Shri Jaswant Singh, Leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party in Rajya 
Sabha and the Leader of the Opposition, Rajya Sabha, under rule 7(3) of the said Rules, on 
January 5, 2006, requesting them to forward their comments on the petition to him within 
seven days from the receipt of the same. 
Shri Jaswant Singh, in his comments, dated the 9th Janauary, 2006, agreed with the 
contention of the petitioner and contended that Shri Jai Narain Prasad Nishad, who had been 
elected to the Rajya Sabha from the State of Bihar as a candidate of the Bharatiya Janata 
Party resigned voluntarily from it. Even if Shri Nishad had not formally resigned from the 
Party, his conduct with regard to his campaining ag anist the party, could he, in itself, a 
sufficient evidence to prove that he has voluntarily given up the membership of the Bharatiya 
Janata Party and, therefore, deserves to be disqualified. 
Shri Jai Narain Prasad Nishad, in his comments, dated the 12th January, 2006, disagreed 
with the charges made agaisnt him. He, inter alia, stated that he had tendered his resignation 
from the primary membership of the party on the 18th October, 2005, in an agitated mental 
condition, which he later withdrew by his letter da ted 17th November, 2005. Shri Nishad 
requested the Chairman, Rajya Sabha, that the petition be dismisssed as the conduct an acts 
as alleged against him by Shrimati Swaraj were condoned by party as is evident by its own 
actions such as issuing him SMS messages for attending party meetings or to act according 
to those messages. The party also continued to take  from his a monthly subscription of 
Rs. 1200 and the last subscription was taken on the 10th December, 2005. 

Government  [15 APRIL 2008]  Bill 141  
After considering the comments of Shri Jaswant Singh and Shri Jai Narain Prasad 
Nishad in relation to the petition, the then Chairman was satisfied, having regard to the 
nature and circumstances of the case that it was necessary to refer the petition to the 
Committee of Privileges of Rajya Sabha and he referred the petition to the Committee 
of Privileges on February 21, 2006, for making a preliminary inquiry and submitting a 
report to him.  
The Committee of Privileges submitted its Report to me on 20th November, 2007.  
On receipt of this Report, I forwarded a copy threreof to Shri Jai Narain Prasad Nishad 
and gave him opportunities to appear before me on January 8, March 11 and March 26, 
2008, to represent his case and to be heard in person, but he did not appear on the scheduled 
dates and time. Shri Nishad was thus given a reasonable opportunity to represent his case 
and to be heard in person in terms of Rule 7(7) of the Members of Rajya Sabha 
(Disqualification on ground of Defection) Rules, 1985.  
Taking into account the facts of the case and the report of the Committee of Privileges 
and in accordance with the provisions of article 102(2) read with the Tenth Schedule to the 
Constitution of India, I decided and declared by an order as follows:  
* 
"In exercise of the powers conferred upon me under article 102(2) read with paragraph 
6 of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution of India, I, Mohammad Hamid Ansari, 
Chairman, Rajya Sabha, hereby decide that Shri Jai Narain Prasad Nishad, an elected 
Member of the Rajya Sabha from the State of Bihar, by voluntarily giving up his 
membership of the Bharatiya Janata Party, his original political party, has become subject 
to disqualification for being a Member of the Rajya Sabha in terms of paragraph 2(1 )(a) 
of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution of India."  
Accordingly, Shri Jai Narain Prasad Nishad has ceased to be a Member of the Rajya 
Sabha with effect from 26th March, 2008.
